help.command.app.detail: Requires a release-managed CLI at /usr/local/bin/nagi. App install and uninstall change only the App; app update updates the whole installation.
help.command.app.install.detail: Downloads and verifies the release matching the current CLI version by default. TAG selects another release. Installs only the App; leaves binaries, profiles, engine, and login service unchanged. Administrator authorization may be required.
help.command.app.install.summary: Install the macOS menu bar App
help.command.app.status.detail: Reads the local installation record; does not contact GitHub or require mihomo.
help.command.app.summary: Manage the macOS menu bar App
help.command.app.uninstall.detail: Quit the App and disable its login item first. Preserves the CLI, mihomo, profiles, and engine service. Administrator authorization may be required.
help.command.app.uninstall.summary: Remove only the menu bar App
help.command.app.update-error.detail: Returns a redacted error string, or an empty error when no failure is pending. Does not require an installation record or running engine.
help.command.app.update-error.summary: Read and clear the last background update failure
help.command.app.update.detail: Alias of update for an installation that includes the App. Downloads the latest release unless TAG is supplied. Quit the App first.
help.command.app.update.summary: Update Nagi including the installed App
help.command.completion.candidates.detai: Lists local names (rules belong to the selected profile), eligible proxy groups in a named profile, or live proxy and provider names; URLs are excluded.
help.command.completion.detail: Prints a shell script or local/live completion candidates.
help.command.config.detail: Validate, print, or safely reload the selected profile. Use `config reload` for a running engine.
help.command.config.reload.detail: Validates the selected profile, then asks a running mihomo instance to reload it.
help.command.config.validate.detail: Runs mihomo -t against the selected profile; requires a mihomo executable.
help.command.connections.close.detail: Closes one connection by its mihomo ID.
help.command.connections.close.hint: Run `nagi connections list` to find IDs.
help.command.connections.detail: Reads or closes active connections from a running engine.
help.command.connections.list.detail: Shows a snapshot of active connections.
help.command.connections.show.detail: Shows one active connection, metadata, counters, and proxy chain.
help.command.connections.show.hint: Run `nagi connections list` to find IDs.
help.command.diagnostics.detail: Checks executable, profile, listeners, DNS, proxy control API, permissions, and controller exposure. Output is redacted.
help.command.dns.check.detail: Inspects the selected effective DNS configuration and queries the running mihomo resolver.
help.command.dns.check.summary: Check DNS configuration and mihomo API
help.command.dns.detail: Configures selected-profile DNS in a separate local override; inspects mihomo DNS through its private control API.
help.command.dns.exception.add.detail: Maps a domain suffix to a DoH URL or an explicitly requested plaintext IP server.
help.command.dns.exception.detail: Exceptions route a domain suffix to an explicit server; plaintext IP servers are allowed only here.
help.command.dns.exception.remove.detail: Removes the selected domain suffix from local DNS policy.
help.command.dns.flush.detail: Requests mihomo to clear its DNS cache; requires a running control API.
help.command.dns.query.detail: Queries the running mihomo resolver over the private control socket.
help.command.dns.set.detail: Saves HTTPS DoH URLs. Proxy binds primary DoH to a named non-direct node or group; bootstrap and proxy-node resolution use direct IP-address DoH. --bootstrap overrides the DNSPod DoH defaults. No plaintext fallback is configured.
help.command.dns.status.detail: Reports configured upstreams, IPv6, TUN, and configuration risks.
help.command.dns.tun.detail: Stores TUN auto-route, strict-route, and port 53 hijack settings; actual activation may require platform privileges.
help.command.dns.tun.off.detail: Disables TUN in the selected profile override.
help.command.dns.tun.on.detail: Configures TUN auto-route, strict-route, and port 53 hijack for IPv4 and IPv6.
help.command.doctor.detail: Checks local paths, mihomo executable, selected profile, process marker, and Unix Socket API without changing files. Exit status is zero for a completed report; inspect healthy and checks for problems.
help.command.lan.detail: Changes runtime allow-lan and bind address. Enabling defaults to all interfaces; supply an explicit local IP to restrict listening.
help.command.lan.enable.detail: Binds to all interfaces by default; ADDRESS must be a local IPv4 or IPv6 address.
help.command.logs.detail: Shows recent lines or follows newly appended log lines until interrupted.
help.command.logs.follow.detail: Streams newly appended log lines until interrupted.
help.command.menu.detail: Browse and run common commands using a line-oriented menu. Requires terminal input and output; use ordinary commands or --json for automation.
help.command.mode.detail: Reads or changes temporary runtime mode, or explicitly persists a mode in the selected profile.
help.command.ports.detail: Reports HTTP, HTTPS, SOCKS, and mixed listener ports from the running engine.
help.command.ports.status.detail: HTTP and HTTPS share mihomo's HTTP proxy port; mixed accepts both HTTP and SOCKS.
help.command.privileged-helper.detail: Installs a system helper with administrator privileges and selects whether Nagi uses it for mihomo lifecycle and control.
help.command.privileged-helper.disable.d: Requires the privileged mihomo process to be stopped; then use nagi start.
help.command.privileged-helper.enable.de: Requires an active helper and a stopped user mihomo process; then use nagi start.
help.command.privileged-helper.install.d: Requires sudo and a root-owned installed Nagi executable at /usr/local/bin/nagi.
help.command.privileged-helper.status.de: Reports system helper installation and the selected engine backend.
help.command.privileged-helper.uninstall: Requires sudo; stop mihomo and disable the privileged backend first.
help.command.profile.backup.detail: Copies the source YAML to profiles/NAME.yaml.bak.
help.command.profile.detail: Profile names use letters, digits, _ or -, up to 128 characters.
help.command.profile.diff.detail: Shows changed lines against another profile or the latest backup (default).
help.command.profile.export.detail: Writes the source YAML to a new file with private permissions; refuses to overwrite an existing file.
help.command.profile.import.detail: Validates and saves a local YAML file, up to 8 MiB. Use profile use to select it.
help.command.profile.import.hint: Run `nagi profile list` to see existing names.
help.command.profile.list.detail: Lists available profiles and marks the current selection.
help.command.profile.override.apply-defa: Copies safe local runtime settings from profiles/default.yaml onto NAME; subscription nodes, groups, rules, and Nagi-managed fields remain unchanged; an enabled TUN stays enabled. On first use, select a target profile proxy group for default DNS; later uses reuse the saved group unless changed explicitly.
The default profile and named target group must exist.
help.command.profile.override.clear.deta: Removes the user-owned override and reloads the selected running profile.
help.command.profile.override.default-st: Reports whether the saved default overlay still matches the profile override.
help.command.profile.override.detail: Stores a YAML mapping separately and applies its keys over the source profile.
help.command.profile.override.restore-de: Restores the local override saved by apply-default; refuses if the override changed since applying.
help.command.profile.override.set.detail: Validates and saves a YAML mapping, up to 8 MiB; reloads the selected running profile.
help.command.profile.remove.detail: Removes an unselected local profile, its backup, local overrides, custom rules, and saved proxy choices; keeps subscriptions and their caches.
help.command.profile.remove.hint: Run `nagi profile list` to see profile names.
help.command.profile.restore.detail: Validates and writes profiles/NAME.yaml.bak; reloads if selected and running.
help.command.profile.use.detail: Validates and activates an existing profile with its own custom rules; reloads a running engine.
help.command.profile.use.hint: Run `nagi profile list` to find a profile name.
help.command.proxy.auto.detail: Clears the fixed node of a URLTest or Fallback group and removes its saved choice.
help.command.proxy.auto.hint: Run `nagi proxy groups` to find an automatic group.
help.command.proxy.delay.detail: Measures an HTTP(S) URL through a proxy node. URL defaults to https://www.gstatic.com/generate_204 and timeout to 5000 ms.
help.command.proxy.delay.hint: Run `nagi proxy groups` to find a node name.
help.command.proxy.delays.detail: Measures all nodes in a group and sorts successful results by ascending latency. Omitted URL and timeout use the effective group settings (fallback: https://www.gstatic.com/generate_204, 5000 ms). Explicit arguments override them; URLTest uses its native configured URL.
help.command.proxy.delays.hint: Run `nagi proxy groups` to find a group name.
help.command.proxy.detail: Adds persistent providers to the selected profile; reads live proxy groups and providers and measures delay.
help.command.proxy.groups.detail: Lists groups in the current profile's order with their live selections.
help.command.proxy.healthcheck.detail: Reads or changes local configuration while offline. Subscription settings can be saved before first apply; associated profiles validate and reload only when selected and running. Provider and group schedulers may differ.
help.command.proxy.healthcheck.reset.det: Removes only the local interval setting while retaining unrelated overrides.
help.command.proxy.healthcheck.set.detai: SECONDS must be 1..31536000. Changes interval only; provider enable and URL remain unchanged.
help.command.proxy.healthcheck.show.deta: Reports interval, test URL origin, sources, lazy setting, and scheduling caveats without probing nodes. --full-url includes the complete saved test URL and read-only inherited-value previews for editing.
help.command.proxy.healthcheck.summary: Manage configured healthcheck intervals and test URLs
help.command.proxy.healthcheck.url.detai: Changes only native healthcheck URLs, independently of intervals.
help.command.proxy.healthcheck.url.reset: Removes only the local URL setting.
help.command.proxy.healthcheck.url.set.d: URL must be absolute HTTP(S), without userinfo or fragment. Inspection shows the origin by default; show --full-url returns the complete test URL.
help.command.proxy.provider.add.detail: Adds a provider to the selected profile local override and attaches it to GROUP. Creates a select group with DIRECT fallback if absent. NAME uses 1..128 ASCII letters, digits, _ or -; GROUP permits internal spaces. URL must be absolute HTTP(S) without userinfo or fragment. SECONDS defaults to 3600 (1..31536000), or off to disable automatic downloads. Optional --test-url URL sets only the provider healthcheck URL; otherwise uses the target automatic group's healthcheck URL and requests an immediate native healthcheck after a running reload, without separate check output. mihomo downloads and healthchecks nodes; routing rules remain unchanged. Reloads only when running.
help.command.proxy.provider.add.hint: Run `nagi proxy groups` to find a running group, or choose a new GROUP name.
help.command.proxy.provider.detail: Adds provider configuration through the selected profile override; inspections, updates, and healthchecks use mihomo APIs.
Asks mihomo to start its provider healthcheck.
help.command.proxy.provider.interval.det: Changes downloads independently of latency checks. Off disables automatic downloads.
help.command.proxy.provider.interval.res: Retains the provider URL and healthcheck settings.
help.command.proxy.provider.interval.set: SECONDS must be 1..31536000, or off. Validates and reloads only when running.
help.command.proxy.provider.remove.detai: Removes the provider definition and all group use references from the selected profile and local override. Retains groups and routing rules. Validates and reloads if running; failure restores prior settings. NAME is printable, 1..128 bytes, without surrounding whitespace; COMPATIBLE is reserved.
help.command.proxy.provider.remove.hint: Inspect the selected profile and override for provider names while stopped.
help.command.proxy.provider.show.detail: Reports redacted provider metadata and node names.
help.command.proxy.provider.update.detai: Asks mihomo to download the provider again.
help.command.proxy.providers.detail: Lists provider names, types, update time, and node names without revealing URLs or credentials.
help.command.proxy.restore.detail: Restores available saved choices for the selected profile and reports missing groups or nodes.
help.command.proxy.restore.hint: Run `nagi proxy groups` to see live selections.
help.command.proxy.search.detail: Lists case-insensitive node-name matches by group.
help.command.proxy.search.hint: Run `nagi proxy groups` to inspect all nodes.
help.command.proxy.select.detail: Selects a node in a group and saves the choice for the selected profile.
help.command.proxy.select.hint: Run `nagi proxy groups` and `nagi proxy show GROUP` to find names.
help.command.proxy.show.detail: Shows one group and its available nodes.
help.command.proxy.show.hint: Run `nagi proxy groups` to find a group name.
help.command.proxy.tailscale.add.detail: NAME is a new printable proxy name (1..128 bytes; spaces allowed). EXIT_NODE is a Tailscale exit IP, name, or auto selector. Omit KEY_FILE to paste the Auth Key interactively with normal terminal echo. Use --auth-key-stdin for bounded stdin input, or keep KEY_FILE for scripts. Keys contain one nonempty printable value, at most 16384 bytes; key-file symlinks are rejected. --hostname sets the Tailscale device hostname; --control-url selects an HTTPS Headscale service (default https://controlplane.tailscale.com). Saves a full local node snapshot, validates, and reloads only when running. Subscription apply retains ordinary local settings and nodes; nodes captured by an entire-subscription binding remain managed. Saving or reloading does not establish login.
help.command.proxy.tailscale.add.hint: Run `nagi proxy tailscale list` or `nagi proxy tailscale targets` to discover names.
help.command.proxy.tailscale.bind.detail: Sets a node dialer-proxy or provider override.dialer-proxy to NAME. Provider binding affects ALL nodes, including future refreshes, without changing the download proxy. Existing non-Tailscale front proxies and dependency cycles are refused; Tailscale bindings may be reassigned. Multiple targets of the same kind are saved together with one validation and reload; any failure rolls back the batch. Entire-subscription bindings persist separately, survive explicit apply and scheduled refresh, and include future nodes. Apply the subscription to the selected profile first; binding never applies it implicitly. While a policy is active, unbind it before changing individual node/provider bindings or adding/removing Tailscale nodes.
help.command.proxy.tailscale.bind.hint: Run `nagi proxy tailscale list` or `nagi proxy tailscale targets` to discover names.
help.command.proxy.tailscale.bind.summar: Chain nodes, providers, or a subscription through Tailscale
help.command.proxy.tailscale.detail: Offline inspection reads the selected effective profile. Mutations validate and save ordinary overrides or a persistent entire-subscription policy, reloading only when running. Control URL defaults to https://controlplane.tailscale.com; key files are regular, nonempty, and at most 16384 bytes. Tailscale identities are retained after removal.
help.command.proxy.tailscale.edit.detail: Updates an existing top-level Tailscale node; at least one option is required. Omitted fields, including Auth Key, are retained. --auth-key prompts for visible paste (blank retains the current key); --auth-key-stdin reads stdin. --auth-key-file retains file input. Choose one key input method, with at most 16384 bytes. --control-url accepts HTTPS Headscale or an empty value for official Tailscale. Saves and validates ordinary node overrides or updates the captured node in an active entire-subscription policy; reloads only when running.
help.command.proxy.tailscale.edit.hint: Run `nagi proxy tailscale list` or `nagi proxy tailscale targets` to discover names.
help.command.proxy.tailscale.hint: Run `nagi proxy tailscale list` or `nagi proxy tailscale targets` to discover names.
help.command.proxy.tailscale.list.detail: Reads top-level Tailscale nodes from the selected effective profile without a running engine; reports key presence only.
help.command.proxy.tailscale.list.hint: Run `nagi proxy tailscale list` or `nagi proxy tailscale targets` to discover names.
help.command.proxy.tailscale.remove.deta: Removes a top-level Tailscale node only after subscription, node, provider, and DNS references are removed. Mihomo validation protects rules and groups. Saves the full node snapshot and reloads only when running; persistent identity state is retained.
help.command.proxy.tailscale.remove.hint: Run `nagi proxy tailscale list` or `nagi proxy tailscale targets` to discover names.
help.command.proxy.tailscale.show.detail: Reads one top-level Tailscale node and its node/provider/subscription bindings while offline. Auth keys and their input file paths are omitted.
help.command.proxy.tailscale.show.hint: Run `nagi proxy tailscale list` or `nagi proxy tailscale targets` to discover names.
help.command.proxy.tailscale.show.summar: Show a Tailscale node and its bindings
help.command.proxy.tailscale.targets.det: Reads eligible top-level proxy nodes and providers from local configuration. Groups, Tailscale nodes, and special outbounds are excluded. A provider binding affects all its nodes. Subscription targets are actual subscription records already applied to the selected profile.
help.command.proxy.tailscale.targets.hin: Run `nagi proxy tailscale list` or `nagi proxy tailscale targets` to discover names.
help.command.proxy.tailscale.unbind.deta: Writes an explicit empty front proxy on a node or provider so a source binding cannot reappear. Provider changes affect ALL nodes, including future refreshes. Multiple targets of the same kind are saved together with one validation and reload; any failure rolls back the batch. Subscription unbind removes its persistent policy while retaining the Tailscale node in the selected profile.
help.command.proxy.tailscale.unbind.hint: Run `nagi proxy tailscale list` or `nagi proxy tailscale targets` to discover names.
help.command.proxy.test.detail: Uses the effective group or provider URL, timeout and expected status; requires an unambiguous individual node.
help.command.proxy.test.group.detail: Uses the group's configured URL, timeout and expected status, resolving only its configured node sources.
help.command.proxy.test.group.hint: Run `nagi proxy show GROUP` to inspect nodes.
help.command.proxy.test.hint: Inspect `nagi proxy groups` or `nagi proxy providers`.
help.command.proxy.test.provider.detail: Uses the provider's configured health-check URL, timeout and expected status.
help.command.proxy.test.provider.hint: Run `nagi proxy provider show PROVIDER` to inspect nodes.
help.command.proxy.test.summary: Measure a node in its source context
help.command.quit.detail: Stops the login monitor and mihomo, restores Nagi-managed system proxy settings, and preserves the next-login startup preference. A later start resumes the monitor.
help.command.quit.summary: Quit Nagi for this login session
help.command.recover.detail: Removes a stale PID/socket marker after an unexpected mihomo exit; it never touches a live process.
help.command.request-rewrite.ca.detail: Commands: status, generate, export, trust. Generation and trust installation are separate explicit operations. No replacement/rotation command.
help.command.request-rewrite.ca.export.d: Public PEM only; never export private key. Refuse existing file, create mode 0600; - writes raw stdout. Reject --json.
help.command.request-rewrite.ca.export.h: Run `nagi request-rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.request-rewrite.ca.generate: Create one private per-user CA. Refuse existing CA. Does not install OS trust.
Run `nagi request-rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.request-rewrite.ca.hint: Run `nagi request-rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.request-rewrite.ca.status.d: Show public CA metadata and assessed OS trust; unknown is not evidence of trust.
help.command.request-rewrite.ca.status.h: Run `nagi request-rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.request-rewrite.ca.status.s: Show local CA and trust metadata
help.command.request-rewrite.ca.trust.de: Commands: install, remove. Affects platform user trust; platform verification is required. Unsupported stores return an actionable error.
help.command.request-rewrite.ca.trust.hi: Run `nagi request-rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.request-rewrite.ca.trust.in: Install public certificate into the supported OS trust store and assess resulting trust. May require platform authorization.
Run `nagi request-rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.request-rewrite.ca.trust.re: Remove OS trust without deleting the private CA. Disable rewriting first; verify trust removal in platform state.
Run `nagi request-rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.request-rewrite.capture.app: Run `nagi request-rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.request-rewrite.capture.bod: Read decoded-byte chunks up to 256 KiB; body data is base64 in JSON.
Run `nagi request-rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.request-rewrite.capture.che: Check prerequisites in order, stopping at the first unmet condition. Read-only; does not start a recorder. Returns readiness even when capture cannot start.
Run `nagi request-rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.request-rewrite.capture.cle: Clear the named retained session history and invalidate cursors.
Run `nagi request-rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.request-rewrite.capture.det: Commands: check, start, status, pause, resume, stop, apps, list, show, body, clear, export, import, fixture, draft. Output contains original credentials and bodies. Requires explicit session start.
help.command.request-rewrite.capture.dra: Read a Selection JSON and derive one validated draft from the original record.
Run `nagi request-rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.request-rewrite.capture.exp: Export raw archive, owner-only exclusive file; - writes stdout. Reject --json.
Run `nagi request-rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.request-rewrite.capture.fix: Create a local preview fixture from complete original snapshots.
Run `nagi request-rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.request-rewrite.capture.hin: Run `nagi request-rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.request-rewrite.capture.imp: Import a native archive as an offline read-only stopped session.
Run `nagi request-rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.request-rewrite.capture.lis: List original records; optional JSON ListOptions contains query, filters, cursor and limit.
Run `nagi request-rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.request-rewrite.capture.pau: Pause this session without interrupting open traffic streams.
Run `nagi request-rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.request-rewrite.capture.res: Resume the named paused session with a new policy revision.
Run `nagi request-rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.request-rewrite.capture.sho: Show complete original URL and header metadata without body bytes.
Run `nagi request-rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.request-rewrite.capture.sta: Start a session; optional JSON StartOptions defines scope, owner and body_limit. Requires running TUN, trusted CA and capture-capable engine; never installs prerequisites.
Run `nagi request-rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
Show recorder session state and limits.
Run `nagi request-rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.request-rewrite.capture.sto: Stop collection and retain original history.
Run `nagi request-rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.request-rewrite.detail: Default off. Configure ordered request, response and WebSocket rules and local scripts; enable requires running TUN, compatible mihomo and a trusted local CA. Commands: status, enable, disable, scripts, rules, import, export, validate, preview, ca, capture, draft.
help.command.request-rewrite.disable.det: Drain and disable runtime rewriting. Retain rule/script data, CA and OS trust. --profile is not accepted.
help.command.request-rewrite.disable.hin: Run `nagi request-rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.request-rewrite.draft.detai: Commands: preview, save. Read a versioned insertion and optional original fixture from private JSON or stdin.
help.command.request-rewrite.draft.hint: Run `nagi request-rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.request-rewrite.draft.previ: Read {base_rule_version,position,rule,fixture?,enable}. Preview runs locally; save inserts atomically with version conflict checking and ordinary activation rollback.
Run `nagi request-rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
Read {base_rule_version,position,rule,fixture?,enable}. Preview runs locally; save inserts atomically with version conflict checking and ordinary activation rollback.
Run `nagi request-rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.request-rewrite.draft.summa: Preview or save a capture-derived rule
help.command.request-rewrite.enable.deta: Requires compatible mihomo, actually running TUN and trusted CA. Does not start TUN or install trust. --profile is not accepted.
help.command.request-rewrite.enable.hint: Run `nagi request-rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.request-rewrite.export.deta: Explicit sensitive raw JSON export; values may contain credentials. Always exports enabled:false, excludes CA and runtime secrets. Refuse existing files, create mode 0600. - writes raw stdout. Reject --json.
help.command.request-rewrite.export.hint: Run `nagi request-rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.request-rewrite.hint: Run `nagi request-rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.request-rewrite.import.deta: Read a complete v2 JSON document (1 MiB maximum). Imported enabled must be false; retain existing enabled intent independently. Validate and replace transactionally.
help.command.request-rewrite.import.hint: Run `nagi request-rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.request-rewrite.preview.det: Explicit sensitive preview: {stage,request,response?,message?}; stage is request, response, exchange, websocket_client or websocket_server. Request includes scheme,host,port,method,path,query,headers,body_base64. No DNS, forwarding or persistence. Maximum 24 MiB encoded fixture and 8 MiB per decoded body. Output contains transformed request values and may contain credentials; it does not prove live coverage.
help.command.request-rewrite.preview.hin: Run `nagi request-rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.request-rewrite.preview.sum: Transform a sensitive local staged fixture
help.command.request-rewrite.rules.add.d: Read one complete rule JSON object from private file or stdin (1 MiB maximum); validate stage, match, operations and script references. Never enables rewriting.
help.command.request-rewrite.rules.add.h: Run `nagi request-rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.request-rewrite.rules.detai: Commands: list, show, add, update, remove, enable, disable, reorder. Inputs contain secret values; ordinary reads show redacted summaries.
help.command.request-rewrite.rules.disab: Disable the rule while retaining its position and data.
Run `nagi request-rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.request-rewrite.rules.enabl: Enable the rule without enabling request rewriting itself.
Run `nagi request-rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.request-rewrite.rules.hint: Run `nagi request-rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
Show IDs, enabled state, match, operation kinds and on_error. Omit operation values and redirect consent.
Run `nagi request-rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.request-rewrite.rules.remov: Run `nagi request-rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.request-rewrite.rules.reord: Read a JSON array containing every rule ID exactly once, including disabled rules.
Run `nagi request-rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
Show one rule summary. Use explicit export for complete sensitive values.
Run `nagi request-rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.request-rewrite.rules.updat: Read one complete rule JSON object with the same ID. Save and activate transactionally when enabled.
Run `nagi request-rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.request-rewrite.scripts.add: Read {id,body_access,source} from a private file or stdin; body_access is none or buffer. Source maximum 64 KiB. Save after validation.
Run `nagi request-rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.request-rewrite.scripts.det: Commands: list, show, source, add, update, remove. Ordinary reads omit source. Referenced scripts cannot be removed.
help.command.request-rewrite.scripts.hin: Run `nagi request-rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.request-rewrite.scripts.lis: Show IDs, body access, source size and referencing rule IDs. Source is omitted.
Run `nagi request-rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.request-rewrite.scripts.rem: Reject removal while any enabled or disabled rule references the script.
Run `nagi request-rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.request-rewrite.scripts.sho: Show metadata and rule references without source.
Run `nagi request-rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.request-rewrite.scripts.sou: Explicit sensitive read: source may contain credentials. Returns the complete script object with sensitive:true; JSON is supported.
Run `nagi request-rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.request-rewrite.scripts.upd: Read the complete script object with the same ID; validate all referencing rules before saving.
Run `nagi request-rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.request-rewrite.status.deta: Show saved intent separately from actual runtime state, versions, CA trust and recovery guidance.
help.command.request-rewrite.status.hint: Run `nagi request-rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.request-rewrite.validate.de: Validate a supplied v2 document or the persisted profile document. No DNS, forwarding, persistence or activation. Read private files or stdin, maximum 1 MiB.
help.command.request-rewrite.validate.hi: Run `nagi request-rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.restart.detail: Restarts mihomo with the selected profile.
help.command.rewrite.ca.detail: Commands: status, generate, export, trust. Generation and trust installation are separate explicit operations. No replacement/rotation command. Also available as nagi request-rewrite; both use the same implementation and JSON contract.
help.command.rewrite.ca.export.detail: Public PEM only; never export private key. Refuse existing file, create mode 0600; - writes raw stdout. Reject --json. Also available as nagi request-rewrite; both use the same implementation and JSON contract.
help.command.rewrite.ca.export.hint: Run `nagi rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.rewrite.ca.generate.detail: Create one private per-user CA. Refuse existing CA. Does not install OS trust. Also available as nagi request-rewrite; both use the same implementation and JSON contract.
help.command.rewrite.ca.generate.hint: Run `nagi rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.rewrite.ca.hint: Run `nagi rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.rewrite.ca.status.detail: Show public CA metadata and assessed OS trust; unknown is not evidence of trust. Also available as nagi request-rewrite; both use the same implementation and JSON contract.
help.command.rewrite.ca.status.hint: Run `nagi rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.rewrite.ca.status.summary: Show local CA and trust metadata
help.command.rewrite.ca.trust.detail: Commands: install, remove. Affects platform user trust; platform verification is required. Unsupported stores return an actionable error. Also available as nagi request-rewrite; both use the same implementation and JSON contract.
help.command.rewrite.ca.trust.hint: Run `nagi rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.rewrite.ca.trust.install.de: Install public certificate into the supported OS trust store and assess resulting trust. May require platform authorization. Also available as nagi request-rewrite; both use the same implementation and JSON contract.
help.command.rewrite.ca.trust.install.hi: Run `nagi rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.rewrite.ca.trust.remove.det: Remove OS trust without deleting the private CA. Disable rewriting first; verify trust removal in platform state. Also available as nagi request-rewrite; both use the same implementation and JSON contract.
help.command.rewrite.ca.trust.remove.hin: Run `nagi rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.rewrite.capture.apps.detail: List observed original process identities. Also available as nagi request-rewrite; both use the same implementation and JSON contract.
help.command.rewrite.capture.apps.hint: Run `nagi rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.rewrite.capture.body.detail: Read decoded-byte chunks up to 256 KiB; body data is base64 in JSON. Also available as nagi request-rewrite; both use the same implementation and JSON contract.
help.command.rewrite.capture.body.hint: Run `nagi rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.rewrite.capture.check.detai: Check prerequisites in order, stopping at the first unmet condition. Read-only; does not start a recorder. Returns readiness even when capture cannot start. Also available as nagi request-rewrite; both use the same implementation and JSON contract.
help.command.rewrite.capture.check.hint: Run `nagi rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.rewrite.capture.clear.detai: Clear the named retained session history and invalidate cursors. Also available as nagi request-rewrite; both use the same implementation and JSON contract.
help.command.rewrite.capture.clear.hint: Run `nagi rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.rewrite.capture.detail: Commands: check, start, status, pause, resume, stop, apps, list, show, body, clear, export, import, fixture, draft. Output contains original credentials and bodies. Requires explicit session start. Also available as nagi request-rewrite; both use the same implementation and JSON contract.
help.command.rewrite.capture.draft.detai: Read a Selection JSON and derive one validated draft from the original record. Also available as nagi request-rewrite; both use the same implementation and JSON contract.
help.command.rewrite.capture.draft.hint: Run `nagi rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.rewrite.capture.export.deta: Export raw archive, owner-only exclusive file; - writes stdout. Reject --json. Also available as nagi request-rewrite; both use the same implementation and JSON contract.
help.command.rewrite.capture.export.hint: Run `nagi rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.rewrite.capture.fixture.det: Create a local preview fixture from complete original snapshots. Also available as nagi request-rewrite; both use the same implementation and JSON contract.
help.command.rewrite.capture.fixture.hin: Run `nagi rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.rewrite.capture.hint: Run `nagi rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.rewrite.capture.import.deta: Import a native archive as an offline read-only stopped session. Also available as nagi request-rewrite; both use the same implementation and JSON contract.
help.command.rewrite.capture.import.hint: Run `nagi rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.rewrite.capture.list.detail: List original records; optional JSON ListOptions contains query, filters, cursor and limit. Also available as nagi request-rewrite; both use the same implementation and JSON contract.
help.command.rewrite.capture.list.hint: Run `nagi rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.rewrite.capture.pause.detai: Pause this session without interrupting open traffic streams. Also available as nagi request-rewrite; both use the same implementation and JSON contract.
help.command.rewrite.capture.pause.hint: Run `nagi rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.rewrite.capture.resume.deta: Resume the named paused session with a new policy revision. Also available as nagi request-rewrite; both use the same implementation and JSON contract.
help.command.rewrite.capture.resume.hint: Run `nagi rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.rewrite.capture.show.detail: Show complete original URL and header metadata without body bytes. Also available as nagi request-rewrite; both use the same implementation and JSON contract.
help.command.rewrite.capture.show.hint: Run `nagi rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.rewrite.capture.start.detai: Start a session; optional JSON StartOptions defines scope, owner and body_limit. Requires running TUN, trusted CA and capture-capable engine; never installs prerequisites. Also available as nagi request-rewrite; both use the same implementation and JSON contract.
help.command.rewrite.capture.start.hint: Run `nagi rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.rewrite.capture.status.deta: Show recorder session state and limits. Also available as nagi request-rewrite; both use the same implementation and JSON contract.
help.command.rewrite.capture.status.hint: Run `nagi rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.rewrite.capture.stop.detail: Stop collection and retain original history. Also available as nagi request-rewrite; both use the same implementation and JSON contract.
help.command.rewrite.capture.stop.hint: Run `nagi rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.rewrite.detail: Default off. Configure ordered request, response and WebSocket rules and local scripts; enable requires running TUN, compatible mihomo and a trusted local CA. Commands: status, enable, disable, scripts, rules, import, export, validate, preview, ca, capture, draft. Also available as nagi request-rewrite; both use the same implementation and JSON contract.
help.command.rewrite.disable.detail: Drain and disable runtime rewriting. Retain rule/script data, CA and OS trust. --profile is not accepted. Also available as nagi request-rewrite; both use the same implementation and JSON contract.
help.command.rewrite.disable.hint: Run `nagi rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.rewrite.draft.detail: Commands: preview, save. Read a versioned insertion and optional original fixture from private JSON or stdin. Also available as nagi request-rewrite; both use the same implementation and JSON contract.
help.command.rewrite.draft.hint: Run `nagi rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.rewrite.draft.preview.detai: Read {base_rule_version,position,rule,fixture?,enable}. Preview runs locally; save inserts atomically with version conflict checking and ordinary activation rollback. Also available as nagi request-rewrite; both use the same implementation and JSON contract.
help.command.rewrite.draft.preview.hint: Run `nagi rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.rewrite.draft.save.detail: Read {base_rule_version,position,rule,fixture?,enable}. Preview runs locally; save inserts atomically with version conflict checking and ordinary activation rollback. Also available as nagi request-rewrite; both use the same implementation and JSON contract.
help.command.rewrite.draft.save.hint: Run `nagi rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.rewrite.draft.summary: Preview or save a capture-derived rule
help.command.rewrite.enable.detail: Requires compatible mihomo, actually running TUN and trusted CA. Does not start TUN or install trust. --profile is not accepted. Also available as nagi request-rewrite; both use the same implementation and JSON contract.
help.command.rewrite.enable.hint: Run `nagi rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.rewrite.export.detail: Explicit sensitive raw JSON export; values may contain credentials. Always exports enabled:false, excludes CA and runtime secrets. Refuse existing files, create mode 0600. - writes raw stdout. Reject --json. Also available as nagi request-rewrite; both use the same implementation and JSON contract.
help.command.rewrite.export.hint: Run `nagi rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.rewrite.hint: Run `nagi rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.rewrite.import.detail: Read a complete v2 JSON document (1 MiB maximum). Imported enabled must be false; retain existing enabled intent independently. Validate and replace transactionally. Also available as nagi request-rewrite; both use the same implementation and JSON contract.
help.command.rewrite.import.hint: Run `nagi rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.rewrite.preview.detail: Explicit sensitive preview: {stage,request,response?,message?}; stage is request, response, exchange, websocket_client or websocket_server. Request includes scheme,host,port,method,path,query,headers,body_base64. No DNS, forwarding or persistence. Maximum 24 MiB encoded fixture and 8 MiB per decoded body. Output contains transformed request values and may contain credentials; it does not prove live coverage. Also available as nagi request-rewrite; both use the same implementation and JSON contract.
help.command.rewrite.preview.hint: Run `nagi rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.rewrite.preview.summary: Transform a sensitive local staged fixture
help.command.rewrite.rules.add.detail: Read one complete rule JSON object from private file or stdin (1 MiB maximum); validate stage, match, operations and script references. Never enables rewriting. Also available as nagi request-rewrite; both use the same implementation and JSON contract.
help.command.rewrite.rules.add.hint: Run `nagi rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.rewrite.rules.detail: Commands: list, show, add, update, remove, enable, disable, reorder. Inputs contain secret values; ordinary reads show redacted summaries. Also available as nagi request-rewrite; both use the same implementation and JSON contract.
help.command.rewrite.rules.disable.detai: Disable the rule while retaining its position and data. Also available as nagi request-rewrite; both use the same implementation and JSON contract.
help.command.rewrite.rules.disable.hint: Run `nagi rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.rewrite.rules.enable.detail: Enable the rule without enabling request rewriting itself. Also available as nagi request-rewrite; both use the same implementation and JSON contract.
help.command.rewrite.rules.enable.hint: Run `nagi rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.rewrite.rules.hint: Run `nagi rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.rewrite.rules.list.detail: Show IDs, enabled state, match, operation kinds and on_error. Omit operation values and redirect consent. Also available as nagi request-rewrite; both use the same implementation and JSON contract.
help.command.rewrite.rules.list.hint: Run `nagi rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.rewrite.rules.remove.detail: Remove exactly one rule transactionally. Also available as nagi request-rewrite; both use the same implementation and JSON contract.
help.command.rewrite.rules.remove.hint: Run `nagi rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.rewrite.rules.reorder.detai: Read a JSON array containing every rule ID exactly once, including disabled rules. Also available as nagi request-rewrite; both use the same implementation and JSON contract.
help.command.rewrite.rules.reorder.hint: Run `nagi rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.rewrite.rules.show.detail: Show one rule summary. Use explicit export for complete sensitive values. Also available as nagi request-rewrite; both use the same implementation and JSON contract.
help.command.rewrite.rules.show.hint: Run `nagi rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.rewrite.rules.update.detail: Read one complete rule JSON object with the same ID. Save and activate transactionally when enabled. Also available as nagi request-rewrite; both use the same implementation and JSON contract.
help.command.rewrite.rules.update.hint: Run `nagi rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.rewrite.scripts.add.detail: Read {id,body_access,source} from a private file or stdin; body_access is none or buffer. Source maximum 64 KiB. Save after validation. Also available as nagi request-rewrite; both use the same implementation and JSON contract.
help.command.rewrite.scripts.add.hint: Run `nagi rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.rewrite.scripts.detail: Commands: list, show, source, add, update, remove. Ordinary reads omit source. Referenced scripts cannot be removed. Also available as nagi request-rewrite; both use the same implementation and JSON contract.
help.command.rewrite.scripts.hint: Run `nagi rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.rewrite.scripts.list.detail: Show IDs, body access, source size and referencing rule IDs. Source is omitted. Also available as nagi request-rewrite; both use the same implementation and JSON contract.
help.command.rewrite.scripts.list.hint: Run `nagi rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.rewrite.scripts.remove.deta: Reject removal while any enabled or disabled rule references the script. Also available as nagi request-rewrite; both use the same implementation and JSON contract.
help.command.rewrite.scripts.remove.hint: Run `nagi rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.rewrite.scripts.show.detail: Show metadata and rule references without source. Also available as nagi request-rewrite; both use the same implementation and JSON contract.
help.command.rewrite.scripts.show.hint: Run `nagi rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.rewrite.scripts.source.deta: Explicit sensitive read: source may contain credentials. Returns the complete script object with sensitive:true; JSON is supported. Also available as nagi request-rewrite; both use the same implementation and JSON contract.
help.command.rewrite.scripts.source.hint: Run `nagi rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.rewrite.scripts.update.deta: Read the complete script object with the same ID; validate all referencing rules before saving. Also available as nagi request-rewrite; both use the same implementation and JSON contract.
help.command.rewrite.scripts.update.hint: Run `nagi rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.rewrite.status.detail: Show saved intent separately from actual runtime state, versions, CA trust and recovery guidance. Also available as nagi request-rewrite; both use the same implementation and JSON contract.
help.command.rewrite.status.hint: Run `nagi rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.rewrite.validate.detail: Validate a supplied v2 document or the persisted profile document. No DNS, forwarding, persistence or activation. Read private files or stdin, maximum 1 MiB. Also available as nagi request-rewrite; both use the same implementation and JSON contract.
help.command.rewrite.validate.hint: Run `nagi rewrite status` for readiness and recovery.
help.command.rules.add.detail: Supports DOMAIN, DOMAIN-SUFFIX, DOMAIN-KEYWORD, DOMAIN-REGEX, IP-CIDR, IP-CIDR6, GEOIP, GEOSITE, PROCESS-NAME, and MATCH (use - for its payload). TARGET is DIRECT, REJECT, or a group name. Saves to the selected profile.
help.command.rules.conflicts.detail: Shows the selected profile's effective rule order, duplicate matchers, and rules shadowed by MATCH.
help.command.rules.connection.detail: Reads the rule and payload recorded by mihomo for an active connection.
help.command.rules.connection.hint: Run `nagi connections list` to find an ID.
help.command.rules.custom.detail: Shows persistent user-owned rules, imported per-rule lists, and rule sets for the selected profile.
help.command.rules.detail: Custom rules belong to the selected profile, are stored separately from its source, and apply before its rules. Switching profiles selects that profile's custom rules.
help.command.rules.disable.detail: Disables a named custom rule, imported per-rule list, or rule set in the selected profile.
help.command.rules.disable.hint: Run `nagi rules custom` to find names.
help.command.rules.enable.detail: Enables a named custom rule, imported per-rule list, or rule set in the selected profile.
help.command.rules.enable.hint: Run `nagi rules custom` to find names.
help.command.rules.import.detail: SOURCE is a local file or an absolute HTTP(S) URL without userinfo (maximum 8 MiB). Imports native YAML rules with their own targets into the selected profile. NAME uses 1..128 ASCII letters, digits, _ or -. Imported rules apply before profile rules; validation or reload failure restores saved rules.
help.command.rules.list.detail: Shows mihomo's ordered active rules, including disabled state and hit counts.
help.command.rules.providers.detail: Shows mihomo rule providers from the running engine.
help.command.rules.remove.detail: Removes a named custom rule, imported per-rule list, or rule set from the selected profile.
help.command.rules.remove.hint: Run `nagi rules custom` to find names.
help.command.rules.test.detail: Requires a running matching mihomo engine. Tests its active rules and rule providers without connecting to the destination; synthetic matching does not update rule counters. Defaults to TCP port 443. TARGET is an ASCII domain or bare IP; --ip supplies a domain's destination address. Mihomo resolves DNS when a rule requires it. Always tests rules even in global/direct mode. Source, inbound, UID, process path and sniffing are unavailable; use rules connection for actual traffic.
help.command.rules.test.hint: Start the matching mihomo engine before testing.
help.command.rules.test.summary: Test a domain or IP against active rules
help.command.service.detail: Installs or removes the per-user launchd Agent or systemd service.
help.command.service.install.detail: Installs a per-user launchd Agent or systemd service.
help.command.service.status.detail: Reports definition, enabled, and active states.
help.command.service.uninstall.detail: Removes the per-user launchd Agent or systemd service.
help.command.start.detail: Starts mihomo with the selected profile; creates the default profile if needed.
help.command.startup.check.detail: Rechecks stale runtime markers, the control socket, and managed OS proxy settings. It only reasserts settings matching the saved baseline and never starts mihomo.
help.command.startup.detail: Inspect or control login autostart and recheck mihomo state after network or sleep/wake changes.
help.command.startup.disable.detail: Disables next-login startup while retaining the service definition, current monitor, and running mihomo.
help.command.startup.enable.detail: Installs the per-user launchd/systemd service if needed and enables login startup.
help.command.startup.status.detail: Reports service installation, enablement, activity, and engine state.
help.command.status.detail: Shows running state, selected profile, PID, and runtime paths.
help.command.stop.detail: Records an explicit stop so the login monitor leaves mihomo stopped; restores system proxy settings managed by Nagi.
help.command.subscription.add.detail: Saves an HTTP or HTTPS URL and optional settings before downloading or activating. Schedule defaults to 3600 seconds; accepts 1..31536000 or off. Test URL must be HTTP(S) without user information or fragment. Names use letters, digits, _ or -, up to 128 characters.
help.command.subscription.apply.detail: Replaces the named profile with cached configuration, retains local settings and node/group changes, clears saved group choices, validates, and selects it. Nagi owns local listeners and controller access.
help.command.subscription.apply.hint: Run `nagi subscription preview NAME` to inspect node changes.
help.command.subscription.detail: Stores URLs and private age identities separately from cached downloads and active profiles.
help.command.subscription.key.detail: Copies a bounded regular identity file into private storage, or clears it. The next encrypted update uses mihomo to decrypt; plaintext feeds are unaffected.
help.command.subscription.key.hint: Run `nagi subscription list` to find a subscription name.
help.command.subscription.key.summary: Set or clear an age identity
help.command.subscription.list.detail: Lists names, refresh/schedule state, cache and applied versions, and profile association without URLs. scheduler_running reports a live scheduler host.
help.command.subscription.preview.detail: Compares cached nodes with the existing profile without changing it.
help.command.subscription.preview.hint: Run `nagi subscription list` to find a subscription name.
help.command.subscription.remove.detail: Removes the saved subscription and its cache.
help.command.subscription.remove.hint: Run `nagi subscription list` to find a subscription name.
help.command.subscription.schedule.detai: Saves 1..31536000 seconds, or off. New subscriptions default to 3600 seconds; legacy entries default to off. A running scheduler downloads when due and may apply the current associated profile.
help.command.subscription.schedule.hint: Run `nagi subscription list` to find a subscription name.
help.command.subscription.update.detail: Validates and caches up to 8 MiB, then reports node changes; does not activate it.
help.command.subscription.update.hint: Run `nagi subscription list` to find a subscription name.
help.command.subscription.watch.detail: Runs foreground updates until interrupted. A second scheduler for this user exits with subscription_error; the login service also hosts this task.
help.command.subscription.watch.hint: Run `nagi subscription list` to inspect due times and failures.
help.command.system-proxy.detail: Uses macOS networksetup. Linux system proxy integration is unsupported; configure applications to use a mihomo listener. Saved macOS settings are restored on stop or engine exit.
help.command.system-proxy.disable.detail: Restores settings saved by system-proxy enable.
help.command.system-proxy.enable.detail: Points OS HTTP and HTTPS proxy settings at the running local mihomo port and saves previous settings for restore.
help.command.system-proxy.status.detail: Reports the active OS proxy settings.
help.command.traffic.detail: Streams upload and download rates and cumulative byte counters from the running mihomo control API.
help.command.traffic.watch.detail: Streams one sample per second from mihomo until interrupted. Text mode prints labeled rates and totals; --json emits one success envelope per sample.
help.command.tun.detail: Reads or changes runtime mihomo TUN mode; requires OS TUN permissions.
help.command.tun.disable.detail: Disables runtime TUN and restores Nagi-managed macOS system DNS; profile reload may re-enable it.
help.command.tun.enable.detail: Enables runtime TUN with auto-route and interface detection; macOS takes over system DNS after the adapter is up and restores it when TUN or mihomo stops. Administrator DNS access is required.
help.command.tun.status.detail: Reports runtime TUN configuration and checks a named OS adapter when available; an up adapter does not prove route capture.
help.command.uninstall.detail: Stops Nagi and removes its login service and managed CLI, mihomo, privileged helper, and App. User data is preserved unless --purge-data is supplied. Quit the App and disable its login item first. Administrator authorization may be required.
help.command.update.detail: Verifies the release before stopping Nagi. Updates CLI, mihomo, and an already installed App, refreshes the default profile, and restores login service preferences. Restarts a previously running engine. TAG defaults to latest. On macOS, --terminal opens Terminal; --app downloads, verifies, and authorizes the update before scheduling installation after the menu App quits. Administrator authorization may be required.
help.command.version.detail: Shows Nagi and mihomo versions, pinned commit, OS, and architecture.
